title: Chocolate Cocoa-Dusted Marshmallows
summary: Light, airy cocoa marshmallow cubes made with beef gelatine and rolled in a cocoa dusting.

ingredients.note: or the equivalent in beef gelatine leaves

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Sift the icing sugar, cornflour and the 2 tbsp of cocoa together for the dusting. Paper the tin, oil the paper thinly and coat it with a third of the brown mixture.

steps.title: Cocoa
steps.text: Stir the boiling water into the 40 g cocoa in the small bowl until you have a smooth, glossy paste, then let it cool.

steps.title: Bloom
steps.text: Pour the cold water into the bowl of the stand mixer, sprinkle on the gelatine and give it 10 min to swell.

steps.title: Syrup
steps.text: Warm the sugar, corn syrup, water and salt in the saucepan, stirring, until the sugar has melted. Then let it bubble undisturbed for 7-9 min and take it off at 116 °C.

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: With the whisk turning slowly, trickle the syrup onto the gelatine, keeping it off the moving whisk. Raise to full speed for 10-12 min, adding the vanilla towards the end, until the mixture is thick, glossy, tripled and just warm to the touch (about 35 °C).

steps.title: Flavour
steps.text: Add the cooled cocoa paste and mix on low for about 20 seconds. Finish by folding with the spatula until the colour is even, without knocking out the air.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Transfer to the tin, smooth it flat and sift on another third of the cocoa dusting.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Let it stand, uncovered, for 6 h or overnight. When ready it feels springy and is no longer tacky.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Turn the slab out onto a board coated with the remaining dusting. Slice into 36 cubes with an oiled knife and toss them in the dusting so every side is brown.

tips: The most common mistake is beating hard after adding the cocoa; it knocks out air and makes dense marshmallows.
Dutch-process cocoa gives a deeper colour and smoother taste than natural cocoa.
Make the cocoa paste first so it has time to cool.
Drop a few into hot milk for an instant chocolate drink.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in an airtight box at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
